docs.title: Install and start tC4
docs.summary: Download translationCore 4 for your computer, install or unpack it, and start it. It opens on the Home screen.
docs.text: The download already has the source texts, the translation helps and the story pictures, so you can start without the internet. Get the file for your computer from the tC4 releases page: the .exe for Windows, the .pkg for macOS (Apple silicon), or the .zip for Linux. Install it: Windows: run the .exe. If Windows warns about an unknown app, choose More info, then Run anyway. Start tC4 from the Start menu. macOS: open the .pkg. If macOS blocks it, open System Settings › Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. Then start translationCore 4 from Applications. Linux: unpack the zip, open a terminal in the translationCore4 folder and run ./start-tc4.sh. Wait for the window. tC4 opens on Home with the heading Your projects. Click + Add a project to start your first project. See The Home screen. The warnings in step 2 appear because the installers are not signed yet. They only appear the first time. Windows says "The backend could not be started": install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64), then start tC4 again. Nothing new opens: only one copy of tC4 runs at a time. Starting it again brings back the window that is already open. Linux prints a line about "--no-sandbox": that is normal for the zip. tC4 is still a pre-release. Keep a copy of important work elsewhere.

docs.title: The Home screen
docs.summary: Home lists your projects. From here you open a book, go back to where you stopped, or add a project.
docs.text: Click a book tile on a project card. A book you have not opened before starts in Understand. A book you have worked in opens where you left it. To come back to Home, click the translationCore logo at the top left. To go straight back to the verse you last edited, click the blue banner or Resume →. See Resume where you left off. The project you used last is always at the top of the list. The line under a project's name shows its language code, how many books it has, and whether it is only on this computer or shared on Door43. Click + Add a project, then choose one of the three cards. New Bible starts a new Bible translation. See Create a Bible project. New Open Bible Stories starts the 50 stories. See Start an Open Bible Stories project. Import a project brings in work from translationCore 3, USFM files or a Scripture Burrito. See Import a project. To close the dialog without choosing, press Esc or click ✕. Settings on the card opens Project settings: the checking language, text direction and script font. See Project settings. Add a book adds another book to the project. Share on Door43 uploads a copy of the project to Door43. See Share to Door43. Click the round person icon at the top right. The menu is the same on Home and inside a project. Sign in to Door43 so you can share projects. Use the internet turns the internet on or off for translationCore. While it is off, a step that needs the internet asks first. App language changes the language of the menus and buttons. See Change the app language. Report a problem opens a form that sends a message to the unfoldingWord help desk. About translationCore shows the version and the license.

docs.title: Understand, Translate and Check — the three modes
docs.summary: Every open project has three modes. Understand the passage, Translate it, then Check it — in any order.
docs.text: Your place in the book stays the same when you switch, and Open Bible Stories projects have the same three modes. Open a book or story from Home. Click Understand, Translate or Check in the middle of the top bar. The one you are in is filled in. Understand: read the passage with its notes, word links and questions, and write your own comments. See Read a passage before you translate. Translate: draft your translation beside the source texts. See The Translate screen. Check: check your draft with Translation Notes and Translation Words, align words, and preview the book. See Choose a checking tool. Many teams go in that order, but you can switch at any time. A book or story you open for the first time starts in Understand. After that, tC4 opens it in the mode you used last. Check goes back to the checking tool you used last. To pick another one, click ← All checking tools at the top left. Switching modes saves a checkpoint if anything changed. See Saving and checkpoints. Exporting is not a separate mode. It is in Check › Community Checking. See Export a book as PDF.

docs.title: Saving and checkpoints
docs.summary: tC4 saves as you work. The indicator at the top right shows whether your last change was saved, and offers Retry if it wasn't.
docs.text: There is no Save button for the project: each verse, check decision, alignment or comment is saved when you finish it. Finish an edit, for example click Save verse after drafting a verse. Look at the top right. Saving… changes to Saved when your work is stored. If it shows Save failed — retry, click Retry. If Retry keeps failing, copy your text somewhere safe before you close tC4. See When a save fails. Indicator Meaning Saved Everything you did is saved. Saving… A save is running. Unsaved changes An editor is still open with text that is not saved yet. Save failed — retry A save did not work. Click Retry. Checkpoint not saved Your work is saved, but the project checkpoint did not finish. Click Retry. A checkpoint is a saved version of the whole project. tC4 makes one when you change mode or leave the project, if something changed. If a checkpoint fails as you leave, Home shows a warning; open the project again and tC4 tries again. Before you close tC4, check that the indicator says Saved.

docs.title: Resume where you left off
docs.summary: The banner at the top of Home takes you back to the last place you changed something, in the mode you were using.
docs.text: It shows the project, the book and chapter (or the story), and the start of what you last changed. On Home, find the dark blue banner under Your projects. Click the banner or its Resume → button. tC4 opens that book and chapter in the mode you used last: Understand, Translate, or Check with the same checking tool. The banner follows your last change, not the last book you opened. Opening a book just to read it doesn't move the banner. A checking decision counts as a change, so after you mark an item in Check, Resume takes you back to that checking tool. Each book tile and story tile on Home also remembers where you were in that book or story. For a story, Resume opens the story at the top. Scroll down to the frame named in the banner. The quote is shortened, so it can stop in the middle of a word. Resume is kept on this computer only. It does not follow you to another computer.

docs.title: Switch project or go back Home
docs.summary: Click the project name at the top left to leave the project and go back to Home, where you can open another project or book.
docs.text: The top left always shows the project you have open, with its initials, name and language code. With a project open, click the project name at the top left. Its tooltip says Switch project. Home opens. If you changed anything, tC4 saves a checkpoint as you leave. Click a book or story tile in any project to open it. To move to another book in the same project, you don't need Home: use the book list on the left of Translate or Understand. See Open a book and move between chapters.

docs.title: Create a Bible project
docs.summary: Create a new, empty Bible translation project. You add books right after.
docs.text: "You'll add books next. Everything here can be changed later." On Home, click + Add a project, then New Bible (1). Type a Bible name, for example Kanuri Bible. Type the Language name and the language Code, for example Kanuri and knc. Choose Left to right or Right to left. Leave Checking language on English. It comes with the app, so you don't need to download anything. Click Create Bible →. The Add a book dialog opens. Continue with Add a book. To cancel, click Cancel or the ✕. Nothing is saved. The name needs at least one plain letter or digit, because it also names the project folder. If that folder already exists, choose another name. Script font sets the font your translation is shown in. Versification is the verse-numbering scheme; most projects keep the default. If a language code is refused, try the code for your specific language, for example knc for Central Kanuri rather than kau. Wait a moment after clicking into a field before you type, then check the name. The first letters can be lost. You can change text direction and font later in Project settings. The name and language can't be changed yet.

docs.title: Add a book
docs.summary: Add one book, or several at once, to a Bible project.
docs.text: The English drafting sources come with tC4, so you can start without an internet connection. On Home, click the Add a book tile on your project card. Click Start a blank book. Choose the book in the Book list (1). To add several books, click Choose several at once → (2) and click each book. Pick one book → goes back to the list. Click Create book (3), or Create {n} books. The new book opens in Understand at chapter 1, so you can read the passage and its helps first. To cancel, click ← Back or the ✕. Nothing is added. A book that is already in the project shows ✓ and can't be picked again. The first step also offers Add books from USFM files: "Choose one or more USFM files. Each file becomes a book, with the file's text as its draft." Practise with a short book such as Titus, Philemon or 3 John. Book introductions can't be drafted yet. Removing a book isn't possible yet either.

docs.title: Open a book and move between chapters
docs.summary: Click a book tile on Home to open it. Inside the project, the book list on the left moves you between books and chapters.
docs.text: Each book remembers where you were, so a tile takes you back to the same place. On Home, click a book tile, for example Titus. A book you haven't opened before starts in Understand. In the list on the left, click a chapter number (1). To open another book of the project, click its name in the list. If the list is hidden, click the Toggle book list button (2) next to the chapter heading. The heading above the text (for example "Titus 1") tells you where you are. The percentage under each book shows how much of it is drafted. A large project can show Opening the project… for a moment while tC4 reads its saved work.

docs.title: Import a project (translationCore 3, USFM or Scripture Burrito)
docs.summary: Bring existing work into tC4 as a new project, from translationCore 3 project zips, USFM files or a Scripture Burrito zip.
headings: If the import button stays grey
docs.text: Each import creates a new project. Nothing on this computer changes until you click Import as a new Bible. On Home, click + Add a project, then Import a project (1). Choose the kind of file: translationCore 3 project, USFM files or Scripture Burrito. Drop your files on the drop area, or click it to choose them. Remove a wrong file with its ✕. Click Review files →. Read the review. A green dot means all is well. An orange dot means you need to act. For a translationCore 3 project, choose Look up on Door43 (needs the internet) or Use installed versions (1). Check the Bible name and Language code and change them if needed. Click Import as a new Bible. Home shows "{name} was imported", and the new card has an Imported badge. To cancel, click Cancel or the ✕. Nothing is created. The name is already used. Type another Bible name. USFM files have no language code. Type it yourself, for example es or es-419. A file is damaged. A red "This file cannot be imported" box gives the reason. Nothing can be imported from that file. See Messages that protect your project. Each USFM file must be one book and start with an \id line. All translationCore 3 zips in one import must be the same language. A Scripture Burrito exported from tC4 also brings its alignments and checking decisions. See Export a project as a Scripture Burrito. An imported USFM project has no source texts yet. Add them in Project settings. The "was imported" message stays until you close it with its ✕. To add a book to a project you already have, use Add a book › Add books from USFM files.

docs.title: Export a book as PDF
docs.summary: Make a print-ready PDF of the open book, laid out with your page setup.
docs.text: The file name carries the book code and today's date. Open the book and click Check. If a checking tool opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. On the Community Checking card, click Open →. Optional: set the page setup (paper size, columns, spacing). See Community Checking preview and page setup. Click Export (1), then Export PDF (2). Keep the suggested file name or type another, then save. The panel shows "Saved <file name>". To cancel, close the save window. No file is made. Undrafted verses print as "[ verse not yet drafted ]". Undrafted chapters at the start or end are left out. If nothing in the book is drafted, tC4 says so and makes no file. The paper size and spacing aren't remembered. Set them each time. Footnotes aren't printed yet. On Linux the save window is the system file window and opens in your Downloads folder. If you can't see its Save and Cancel buttons, press Enter to save or Esc to cancel.

docs.title: Export a book as USFM (aligned or plain)
docs.summary: Save the open book as a USFM file, with your word alignments or as plain text.
docs.text: USFM is the standard text format for Bible translations. Open the book and click Check. If a checking tool opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. On the Community Checking card, click Open →. Click Export (1), then USFM, aligned (2) or USFM, plain. Keep the suggested file name or type another, then save. The panel shows "Saved <file name>". To cancel, close the save window. No file is made. USFM, aligned includes your links to the original language, for tools that read alignments. Align the verses first. See Link your words to the source. USFM, plain is just your text. Your project doesn't change. A joined verse span is written as one verse, for example \v 2-3. Undrafted verses are written as ___. The header lines (\h, \toc1–\toc3, \mt) contain the book code, such as TIT, not the book name. Edit them if another program needs the name. On Linux the save window is the system file window and opens in your Downloads folder. If you can't see its Save and Cancel buttons, press Enter to save or Esc to cancel.

docs.title: Export a project as a Scripture Burrito
docs.summary: Save the whole project, with alignments and checking decisions, as one Scripture Burrito zip.
docs.text: Use it to keep a safe copy, move the project to another computer, or give it to another Scripture Burrito tool. Open the book and click Check. If a checking tool opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. On the Community Checking card, click Open →. Click Export (1), then Scripture Burrito (.zip) (2). Keep the suggested file name or type another, then save. The panel shows "Saved <file name>". To cancel, close the save window. No file is made. The zip holds every book of the project, not only the open one. Open Bible Stories projects have the same menu item. To bring the zip back, use + Add a project › Import a project › Scripture Burrito. See Import a project. To put a project on Door43, use Share on Door43 on its Home card. See Share to Door43. On Linux the save window is the system file window and opens in your Downloads folder. If you can't see its Save and Cancel buttons, press Enter to save or Esc to cancel.

docs.title: The Translate screen
docs.summary: Translate is where you draft. The source text is on the left, your translation is beside it, and the helps are on the right.
docs.text: Each row puts a section of the source text next to your translation of it. Open a book, then click Translate at the top. Pick a chapter in the book list on the left. Choose the source text with the tabs above it: ULT (literal), UST (simplified) or the original language (Greek or Hebrew). The line under the tabs names the text and its version. Choose Section to draft a whole section at once, or Verse to draft one verse at a time. Click Draft section beside the section you want. Type the text, then use Place verse numbers. See Draft a section. Click Save section. To leave the section as it was, click Cancel. The button at the top left of the page shows or hides the book list. At the top right of the page, one button widens the helps panel and the other hides it. Click the first one again to put the panel back to its normal width. The panel shows help for the section you are working on: Notes, Words, Questions, the simplified text (UST) and Comments from Understand. Click a help card and the words it is about are highlighted in the source text. See The helps panel in Translate. Translate remembers your choice of Section or Verse for each project.

docs.title: Source tabs — gateway texts and the original language
docs.summary: Switch the source column between the literal text, the simplified text and the Greek or Hebrew original.
docs.text: Your translation stays the same when you switch; only the source column changes. In Translate, look at the tabs above the source column. Click ULT (the literal text), UST (the simplified text) or Greek. An Old Testament book has Hebrew instead of Greek. The caption under the tabs names the text and its version. The sections follow the selected source. In Titus 1, ULT and UST start with 1–3, while Greek shows the whole chapter as 1–16. Words in curly braces, such as {and}, are part of the source text. They mark words added to make the meaning clear. Some gateway languages name the first two tabs differently, for example GLT and GST. The same tabs are in Understand. If a text is missing, the column says "This source is not available for this book." See Browse and download source texts.

docs.title: Draft a section
docs.summary: Type a whole section as one piece of text, then place the verse numbers. This is the main way to draft in tC4.
docs.text: You type the section straight through, the way you would say it, and add the verse numbers afterwards. In Translate, make sure the switch above your translation says Section. On the row you want, click Draft section {span} at its top right (1). The editor opens in Type mode. Type your translation of the whole section. Click Place verse numbers and put each number where its verse begins. See Place verse numbers. Click Save section. To close the editor without saving, click Cancel. To change a saved section, click its Draft section {span} label again. Clicking the saved text does not open the editor. You can type the verse numbers yourself: start a line with the number, for example 5 no nos salvó…. The first verse number of a section is always at the start. Wait a moment after the editor opens before you type, and check the start of your text before you save. While an editor is open, the Section / Verse switch can't be used. A verse number you leave in the To place box is saved as an empty verse.

docs.title: Place verse numbers
docs.summary: After typing a section, pick up each verse number and click the word where that verse begins.
docs.text: Each verse number is a small orange marker, and numbers you haven't placed yet wait in the To place box. In the section editor, click Place verse numbers. Click a number in the To place box to pick it up. The words where that verse can begin are highlighted. Click the word where the verse begins. Repeat for every number, then click Save section. To go back to typing, click Type. The numbers you placed are kept. Cancel closes the editor without saving. To move a number that is already placed, pick it up from the text and click another word. If a number lands on a nearby word as soon as you pick it up, pick it up again and click the right word. When you pick up a placed number, the box still says "Every verse is placed". Follow the line under it: "Click the word where verse 3 begins". A number can't pass another number, and the first number of the section can't move. Putting a number on the word where another verse begins joins them into a span. See Make or break a verse span.

docs.title: Make or break a verse span
docs.summary: Join two or more verses into one span, such as 2-3, when your language needs to reorder their content. Break the span again the same way. Bible projects only.
docs.text: A verse span (also called a verse bridge) is two or more verses translated as one unit, for example 2-3. Open the section with its Draft section {span} label, type the text, and click Place verse numbers. Pick up the later number, for example 3. Click the word where the earlier verse (2) begins. The tooltip says "Join verse 3 to verse 2 at …". Click Save section. The verses are saved as one span, numbered 2-3. Open the section again, click Place verse numbers, pick up the 3 and click the word where verse 3 should begin. Then click Save section. In Type mode you can also start a line with the span, for example 2-3 …. Making or breaking a span marks the checks and alignments of those verses for review. Nothing is deleted. See Editing a verse you already checked or aligned. Spans can't be made in Verse view. Open Bible Stories have frames, not verse numbers, so they have no spans.

docs.title: Draft or revise one verse
docs.summary: Switch to Verse to draft a single verse, or to fix one verse without opening the whole section.
docs.text: Verse view is handy for small corrections and for translators who prefer to work one verse at a time. In Translate, click Verse in the switch above your translation. For an empty verse, click its dashed Draft verse {n} button. For a drafted verse, click its text. Type in the editor. Click Save verse, or click outside the editor. To throw away your change, click Cancel instead. The helps panel follows the verse you are editing. To make a verse span, use Section view. See Make or break a verse span.

docs.title: Paragraphs and poetry
docs.summary: Start a new paragraph with Enter and indent a poetry line with Tab while you type a section.
docs.text: This works in the section editor's Type mode. Open a section with Draft section {span}. Type your text. Press Enter where a new paragraph begins. At the start of a poetry line, press Tab. Press Tab again for a second level, or Shift+Tab to take an indent back. Place the verse numbers and click Save section. The source text shows its own paragraphs and poetry lines, so you can follow them. Headings, footnotes and other formatting can't be added in the editor yet.

docs.title: The helps panel in Translate
docs.summary: While you draft, the helps panel shows the notes, word links, questions, simplified text and your own comments for the verses in focus.
docs.text: It sits on the right of Translate, next to your draft. If the panel is hidden, click Toggle helps panel at the top right of the chapter. Click a tab. Open a section or verse editor. The panel narrows to the verses you are editing. Notes: translation notes, with links to Translation Academy articles. Words: key terms, each with Read the article →. Questions: questions with answers, to test your draft's meaning. UST: the simplified text of the chapter. Some gateway languages give this tab another name, such as GST. Comments: comments you wrote in Understand. It says "Nothing in this chapter." when there are none. Point at a card to highlight its words in the source; click it to keep the highlight. Long notes have Show more and Show less. To give the panel more room, click Widen the helps panel (⇤) next to it. Click it again to restore the width. Each help is explained in the Understand section.

docs.title: Editing a verse you already checked or aligned
docs.summary: When you change a verse that has check decisions or alignments, tC4 flags them for review. Nothing is deleted.
docs.text: Checks and alignments are tied to the exact words of a verse, so when those words change tC4 marks what may no longer fit. Change a verse in Translate that you already checked or aligned. Go to Check and open the checking tool. A notice at the top says how many decisions need review. Click the Invalid filter to see those items, and decide each one again. Open Align for the verse. Words you changed are back in the word bank. Place them and click ✓ Mark valid again. A check decision whose words changed becomes Invalid. It is kept, not deleted. In Align, links to the words you didn't change are kept. The verse shows as to do again. Making or breaking a verse span has the same effect on those verses. A checking tool may reopen at the item you were on. Use the Invalid filter to find every item that needs review.

docs.title: Read a passage before you translate
docs.summary: Understand shows the source passage section by section, with its helps beside it and a box for your own comments.
docs.text: Many teams read and talk about a passage here before they draft it. Open a book, then click Understand at the top. Pick a chapter in the book list on the left. Choose the source text with the ULT or UST tab. Projects with a Spanish checking language show GLT and GST instead. Next to Comment by, choose Section to read a section at a time, or Verse for one verse at a time. Read the helps on the right: Notes, Words, Questions and UST. Click a help card and the words it is about are highlighted in the passage. To keep a thought for later, type it in the comment box under the section. See Write a user comment. A small green dot on a section means you wrote a comment there. Sections follow the breaks in the source text, so a chapter can split differently in different gateway languages. Your choice of Section or Verse is shared with Translate. Understand shows the gateway texts. The Greek or Hebrew is in Translate and Check.

docs.title: Translation notes and Translation Academy articles
docs.summary: Translation notes explain hard phrases verse by verse. Each note can link to a Translation Academy article that teaches the translation issue behind it.
docs.text: Many notes link to a Translation Academy article, a short lesson about a translation issue such as metaphors or abstract nouns. In Understand, click a section to select it. In the helps panel, click Notes and read the cards. Point at a card to highlight its phrase in the passage. Click Translation Academy → on a note. The article opens under the notes. Close the article with ✕. The first card of a chapter is its introduction. Click Show more to read all of it. Notes are in the project's checking language. If you see "Shown from the English fallback", the notes in that language aren't on this computer, so the English notes are shown. See Checking language. Some introductions show a link written out as text, such as "rc://*/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns". It isn't a button. If an article is missing, the panel says "The pinned resources do not carry the article for this check." The note still shows. The same notes become check items in Check with Translation Notes.

docs.title: Word links (Translation Words)
docs.summary: Word links point out the key biblical terms in the passage and link each to a Translation Words article that defines it.
docs.text: Use them to translate key terms such as grace, apostle or righteous the same way every time. In Understand, select a section. In the helps panel, click Words. Point at a card to see its word in the passage. Click Read the article → on a card (1). The article opens under the cards (2), and the word is highlighted in the passage. Close the article with ✕. Each card shows the word as it appears in the passage and the name of its article. The same terms become check items in Check with Translation Words.

docs.title: Translation questions
docs.summary: Translation questions ask what the passage says. Use them to test whether your translation communicates the meaning.
docs.text: Ask them of someone who reads or hears your translation, and see whether their answers match. In Understand, select a section. (The same tab is in the helps panel in Translate.) Click Questions. Read each question and its answer. If there are no questions, the tab says "Nothing in this chapter." or "Nothing for the verses in focus." They are useful after drafting and during community checking.

docs.title: The simplified text tab
docs.summary: The helps panel can show the meaning-based simplified text next to what you are reading.
docs.text: It says the meaning plainly, which helps when the literal text is hard to follow. In Understand or Translate, open the helps panel. Click UST. Some gateway languages name this tab differently, such as GST. Words in curly braces, such as {write this letter to you, Titus. I}, are part of the simplified text. They mark words added to make the meaning clear. You can also show the simplified text in the main source column with the UST source tab. Open Bible Stories have no simplified text, so there is no tab for it.

docs.title: Write a user comment
docs.summary: Write down what a passage means, who is speaking, and what will be hard to translate. Your comments are saved with the project and shown in Translate.
docs.text: A comment is your own note about a section or verse, and it stays with the project. In Understand, choose Section or Verse next to Comment by (1). Click in the box under the section or verse (2) and type your comment. Click outside the box. The comment is saved; watch the indicator at the top right. Later, in Translate, click Comments in the helps panel to read it. To change a comment, edit the text and click outside again. A saved comment can't be emptied: "A saved user comment cannot be emptied — user comments are permanent in this version." Change the text instead. In Section view, if you wrote comments on single verses inside the section, tC4 suggests switching to Verse to see each one. These comments are separate from check comments. See Write a check comment.

docs.title: Choose a checking tool
docs.summary: Check lists the checking tools for the open book and how far you have got in each one.
labels: No items in this book yet
docs.text: Each checking tool takes you through the whole book once, one item at a time. translationCore remembers your place in each tool. Open a book, then click Check at the top. Look at the cards. Each one shows how many items are resolved and which one is next. Click Start checking → on the card you want, or Continue → if you have started. On Community Checking the link is Open →. To come back to this list, click ← All checking tools at the top left of the tool. The next time you click Check, translationCore opens the checking tool you used last. Translation Words: key terms, one at a time. Translation Notes: the places a translation note points to. Align: link your words to the original language. This card counts drafted verses, so a book with nothing drafted says No items in this book yet. Community Checking: read the whole book as a printed page and export it for reviewers. A story project has no Align card. If a card says Needs downloading or Unavailable offline, click Fix this…. See Fix a missing resource. The other tools still work while you fix it. Note: Only drafted verses can be checked. Draft first, then come back.

docs.title: Check with Translation Notes
docs.summary: Go through the hard places in the book, such as figures of speech or abstract nouns, and check how you translated each one.
docs.text: Each item is a note that links to a Translation Academy lesson. Other notes stay in the helps panel. Click Check, then Start checking → on the Translation Notes card. Read What to check. The words it is about are highlighted in the gateway text below. To learn more about the issue, click Learn more under the note. The Translation Academy lesson opens in a panel on the right. Close it with ✕. Under Your translation, tap the word or words that translate the highlighted quote. Choose ✓ Mark valid, Invalid or To do. See Decide on a check item. Click → at the top right to go to the next item. Marking an item does not move you on. To stop, click ← Back to translating at the bottom left. Sort By verse goes through the book in order. By category puts all the notes about one issue together, for example every metaphor. The filters show All, To do, Invalid, Bookmarked or Commented items. See Filter and sort check items. The notes are in your project's checking language. See Change the checking language. If you change a verse after you decided on it, translationCore asks you to look at that decision again. Nothing is lost.

docs.title: Check with Translation Words
docs.summary: Go through every key term in the book, such as God, grace or apostle, and check how you translated each one.
docs.text: Use it to make sure each term is translated the right way, and the same way everywhere it appears. Click Check, then Start checking → on the Translation Words card. Read the term at the top. Click Learn more to read what it means. The article opens in a panel on the right. Close it with ✕. Under Your translation, tap the word or words that translate the highlighted term. Choose ✓ Mark valid, Invalid or To do. See Decide on a check item. Click → at the top right to go to the next item. Marking an item does not move you on. To stop, click ← Back to translating at the bottom left. Next time, Check opens Translation Words where you left it. Sort By word puts every place a term is used together, so you can see whether you translated "grace" the same way each time. By verse goes through the book in order. The filters show All, To do, Invalid, Bookmarked or Commented items. See Filter and sort check items. ⚑ Bookmark marks an item to come back to. ✎ Add a comment leaves a note for your team. See Bookmark a check and Write a check comment. Note: A verse that is not drafted yet cannot be checked. Draft it in Translate first.

docs.title: Decide on a check item (valid, invalid, to do)
docs.summary: For each check, select the words in your translation, then mark the item valid or invalid, or leave it to do.
docs.text: Every item starts as To do until you decide it. Read the highlighted quote in the source. Under Your translation (1), tap the word or words that translate it. Tap again to unselect. Click ✓ Mark valid if the translation is right, or Invalid if something needs fixing (2). Click To do to take a decision back. Click → at the top right (3) to go to the next item, or click any item in the list on the left. Marking an item doesn't move you on, so you can change your mind before you go to the next one. Each decision is saved right away. Your translation shows your words without punctuation, and a word with an apostrophe can look split (for example "God's" as "God s"). Your text in Translate isn't changed. To fix the text, click ← Back to translating. See Editing a verse you already checked or aligned. Use the Invalid filter later to find everything you still need to fix. If you see "This check was not saved. The project's resource changed since this book was checked…", update the resource first, then check again. Nothing was lost.

docs.title: Bookmark a check
docs.summary: Flag a check item to come back to it later, for example to discuss with your team.
docs.text: A bookmark doesn't change the decision. In a checking tool, open the item. Click ⚑ Bookmark. It now reads Bookmarked (1), and the item gets a small flag in the list. Later, click the Bookmarked filter at the top of the list to see every bookmarked item. To remove a bookmark, click Bookmarked again. Add a comment to say why you bookmarked it. See Write a check comment.

docs.title: Write a check comment
docs.summary: Add a note to a check item about what you decided or what to ask your team.
docs.text: Use it to record why you decided something, or a question for a consultant. In a checking tool, click ✎ Add a comment. Type your note in the box My comment on this check. Click Done. The item gets a ✎ in the list and counts under the Commented filter. To close the box without changes, click Hide comment. To remove a comment, click Delete comment. Check comments can be deleted; comments in Understand can't. See Write a user comment.

docs.title: Filter and sort check items
docs.summary: Narrow the list to what still needs work, and change the order of items.
docs.text: The list on the left of a checking tool has filters and a sort switch at the top. Open a checking tool. Click a filter. Each one shows how many items it has. Next to Sort, click one of the two orders. Click an item to open it. When nothing matches, the list says "Nothing matches this filter." The item you had open stays on the right. Filter Shows All every item To do items not decided yet Invalid items marked invalid Bookmarked items with a bookmark Commented items with a comment Translation Words: By word or By verse. In stories: By word or By frame. Translation Notes: By verse or By category. In stories: By frame or By category. Finish a pass with To do, then fix problems with Invalid.

docs.title: Community Checking preview
docs.summary: Read the whole book as a printed page, set up the page, and export a copy for reviewers.
docs.text: Use it to read the book as a whole, or to read it aloud with your community. Click Check, then Open → on the Community Checking card. Scroll the preview. Verses that are not drafted yet show as "[ verse not yet drafted ]". In Page setup, choose Columns (1 or 2), Spacing (Single or Double) and Paper size (A4 or Letter). Turn Drop-cap chapters and Verse numbers on or off. Click Export to save a copy. See Export a book as PDF, Export a book as USFM and Export a project as a Scripture Burrito. To go back, click ← All checking tools. Double spacing leaves room for reviewers to write between the lines. The page setup changes only the preview and the export, not your translation. translationCore does not keep the page setup when you leave this screen. Set it again before you export. Footnotes is greyed out and cannot be turned on yet.

docs.title: Open the Align tool
docs.summary: Align links each word of your translation to the original-language word it translates. Open it from Check.
docs.text: The checking tools use these links to highlight your words, and an aligned USFM export carries them. Click Check, then Start checking → on the Align card. Pick a verse in the verse list on the left. Verses that are not drafted yet are greyed out. Link your words to the word cards. See Link your words to the source. When the verse is done, click ✓ Mark valid. See Mark an alignment done. To leave, click ← All checking tools at the top left, or ← Back to translating at the bottom left. Gateway · ULT aligns to the gateway text you can read. Its words already carry the link to the original language. Original · Greek aligns straight to the Greek words. See Align to the gateway text or the original language. Suggest links is off at first. Turn it on to get links proposed from the verses you have already aligned. See Alignment suggestions. Above the word bank, a count shows how many of the verse's words are placed. How alignment works opens a short explanation. Note: Align is for Bible books. Story projects have no Align card.

docs.title: Link your words to the source
docs.summary: Click a word in the word bank and then the card it belongs under, or drag it there.
docs.text: Each source word has a card, and the words of your verse wait in the word bank above them. In Align, open a verse. Click a word in the word bank (1). The cards get a blue outline, and the word's tooltip says "Now click the card this word belongs under." Click the card it belongs under (2). Or drag the word onto the card. Repeat until your words are placed. The count at the top right of the word bank goes up. Click ✓ Mark valid. See Mark an alignment done. To undo a link, click the placed word. It goes back to the word bank. To unselect a word without placing it, click it again. How alignment works at the top of the verse gives a short reminder. You can mark a verse done even if some words stay in the bank, for example words your language adds. If you change the verse in Translate later, the changed words go back to the word bank. See Editing a verse you already checked or aligned.

docs.title: Align a phrase (merge and split cards)
docs.summary: When several source words are translated together, merge their cards into one phrase card. SPLIT undoes it.
docs.text: Use a phrase card when two or more source words become one word in your language, or a phrase translates a phrase. In Align, drag a word card onto the card next to it. The tooltip says "Drag onto another word card to merge them into a phrase." The two cards become one phrase card. Place your word or words under the phrase card. To undo, click SPLIT on the phrase card. Merge only neighbouring words that belong together. If you had already placed words under the phrase card, check where they are after SPLIT. Click a misplaced word to send it back to the bank, then place it under the right card.

docs.title: Align to the gateway text or the original language
docs.summary: Align to the gateway words you can read (which already carry the link to the original), or directly to the Greek or Hebrew words.
docs.text: Either way, the saved links point to the original language. In Align, open a verse. Click Gateway · ULT or Original · Greek. An Old Testament book shows Original · Hebrew. Link the words as usual. See Link your words to the source. Gateway · ULT: "Align to the gateway text you can read — its words already carry the original-language alignment." Easier if you don't read Greek or Hebrew. A card can hold a gateway phrase, such as "of the chosen people" over ἐκλεκτῶν. Original · Greek or Original · Hebrew: "Align directly to the original-language words." The cards show only the original words. Words you already placed stay where they are when you switch. If the gateway text for a verse has no alignment data, gateway mode says "The gateway lens needs the gateway source text with alignment data for this verse." Use the original-language mode instead.

docs.title: Alignment suggestions
docs.summary: tC4 can learn from the verses you have already aligned and suggest links for the next ones. You confirm or reject each one.
docs.text: Suggestions are based on how you aligned earlier verses in the same testament. Nothing is saved until you confirm it. Align a few verses carefully by hand first. In Align, tick Suggest links in the Suggestions row. The row says "Drawn from N verses you have already aligned". Open a verse and click Suggest. Check each dashed suggestion and click its ✓ to confirm it. Accept all confirms every suggestion, Reject all turns them all down, and Reset clears them. Suggestions can be wrong, especially after only a few hand-aligned verses: words may be placed in the order they come rather than by meaning. Check every one before you confirm it, and don't use Accept all without checking. Confirm or reject the suggestions before you mark the verse done. If nothing fits, it says "Nothing to suggest for the words still in the bank." The setting is remembered for each project on this computer.

docs.title: Mark an alignment done
docs.summary: When a verse is aligned, mark it valid. It counts toward the verses-aligned progress.
docs.text: It means "this verse's alignment is done", even if some words stay in the word bank. Finish linking the words of a verse, and confirm or reject any suggestions. Scroll to the bottom of the verse and click ✓ Mark valid. Go to the next verse with the list on the left or the → arrow at the top right. Marking a verse doesn't move you on. The count at the top of the list ("0 of 9 verses aligned") goes up for each verse you mark. If you edit the verse later, the mark is taken back and the verse needs another look. See Editing a verse you already checked or aligned. Upgrading the Greek or Hebrew text also takes the marks back. See Upgrade scripture texts.

docs.title: Start an Open Bible Stories project
docs.summary: Create a project for translating all fifty Open Bible Stories into your language.
docs.text: Open Bible Stories are 50 short Bible stories, each told in numbered frames with a picture. English stories and helps come with the app. On Home, click + Add a project, then New Open Bible Stories. Type a Project name, the Language name and its Code. Choose the Text direction. Leave Checking language on English. Click Create stories →. The new card appears on Home. Click a story tile (1) to open it. A new story opens in Understand. To cancel, click Cancel or the ✕. Nothing is saved. Wait a moment after clicking into a field before you type, then check what you typed. The first letters can be lost. You can change text direction, font and checking language later in Project settings. The name and language can't be changed yet.

docs.title: Find a story on Home
docs.summary: The stories card shows three stories. Show all 50 to pick any story.
docs.text: Each story is a tile, like a book tile in a Bible project. It shows the story number, title and percent drafted. On Home, find your stories card. It has the OBS badge. Click a tile to open that story, or click Show all 50 stories → (1). Click any story in the grid. To fold the grid again, click Show recent stories only → at the bottom of the card. Resume → at the top of Home reopens the last story you edited.

docs.title: Translate a story
docs.summary: Draft the story title, each frame and the reference line, with the picture and the English story beside you.
docs.text: Stories are drafted part by part: the title, each frame, then the reference. Open a story and click Translate. Click Draft the title (1) and type the title. Click Save. For each frame, click "Draft frame N" (2), look at the picture and the English text, and type your translation. Click Save (1). At the end, click Draft the reference and translate the line "A Bible story from: …". To change a saved part, click its text. To cancel, click Cancel. The story's percent drafted on the left goes up as you save parts. Notes, words and questions for the frame are in the helps panel on the right. Stories have no verse numbers or spans.

docs.title: Understand a story
docs.summary: Read each frame with its picture and the story helps before you translate.
docs.text: It works like reading a passage in a Bible project, frame by frame. Open a story and click Understand. Read the title and each frame with its picture. Click a frame number on the left to jump to it. Read the Notes, Words and Questions on the right. To leave a comment for your team, click the frame's comment box (1), type, then click outside it to save. Click a frame first so the helps panel shows that frame's helps. Story notes are labelled like verses: frame 1's notes say v1, and the title's say v0. A saved comment can't be emptied later. If a comment fails to save, edit the box and click outside it again.

docs.title: Check a story
docs.summary: Check a story with Translation Notes and Translation Words, frame by frame.
docs.text: It works like checking a Bible book, for the open story. Open a story and click Check. If a tool opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. Click Start checking → on Translation Words or Translation Notes. Next to Sort, click By frame (1) to go through the story in order. Tap the words in your translation that match the highlighted word, then click ✓ Mark valid or Invalid (2). Item 1:0 is the story title. Frames are 1:1, 1:2 and so on. An undrafted frame says "This frame is not drafted yet. Draft it first, then return to check." Stories have no alignment. Bookmarks, comments and filters work as for Bible books.

docs.title: Story preview and export
docs.summary: Preview a story as a page with its pictures, choose the layout, and export it for reviewers.
docs.text: Open a story and click Check. If a tool opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. On Community Checking, click Open →. Choose Pictures above or Pictures wrapped (1), and turn Pictures on or off (2). Read the story aloud with your community. To make a copy for reviewers, click Export. See Export stories as PDF or Markdown. Pictures wrapped puts a small picture beside each frame, so more fits on a page. Undrafted frames show as one line, such as "[ frames 3–16 not yet drafted ]", without pictures. Stories have no spacing or paper-size choice. The story PDF is A4, and its first page has only the title.

docs.title: Export stories as PDF or Markdown
docs.summary: Save a printable PDF of your stories, a Story Markdown zip, or a Scripture Burrito.
docs.text: Export PDF: a reading copy for reviewers, with or without pictures. Story Markdown (.zip): the story files for other Open Bible Stories tools. Scripture Burrito (.zip): the whole project. See Export a project as a Scripture Burrito. Open a story and click Check, then Open → on Community Checking. Optional: choose the layout and pictures. See Story preview and export. Click Export (1), then pick a format (2). Keep the suggested file name or type another, then save. The panel shows "Saved <file name>". To cancel, close the save window. No file is made. Draft at least the title or one frame before you export a PDF. To save a second PDF with another layout, change the layout, export again and give it a new name. If you see "The app could not print the PDF with its pictures…", turn Pictures off and export again. On Linux the save window opens in your Downloads folder. If you can't see its buttons, press Enter to save or Esc to cancel.

docs.title: What comes with the app
docs.summary: tC4 comes with English source texts and helps and the Greek and Hebrew texts, so you can translate and check without the internet.
headings: See which version a tool uses
docs.text: Nothing to do: these are ready when you create a project. Resource What it is Version ULT unfoldingWord Literal Text (English) v91 UST unfoldingWord Simplified Text (English) v91 UGNT Greek New Testament v0.34 UHB Hebrew Bible v3.0.0 Translation Notes English notes v91 Translation Words English word articles and links v91 Translation Academy English lessons v91 Translation Questions English questions v91 UGL / UHL Greek and Hebrew lexicons included Open Bible Stories English stories v9 Story notes, word links, questions English story helps v13, v3, v10 Story pictures Pictures for each frame included Open a checking tool from Check. Read the line under the filters (1). A newer app may come with newer versions. For another gateway language, see Download source texts.

docs.title: Download source texts
docs.summary: Download source texts and helps in another gateway language from Door43.
docs.text: A gateway language is the language your team reads the source and helps in. English comes with the app. On Home, click Settings on the project card, then Manage source texts →. The project opens with Get source texts on top. Under Choose your gateway language, click a language (1). If "Turn on the internet?" appears, click Turn on internet. See Working offline. Choose the Book. Check the Package contents. Click a card to leave it out, or again to add it back. Click ⇣ Download package. When it says "✓ {book} · {language} is ready", click Close. To cancel, click Close or the ✕. Nothing is downloaded. Two rows can share a name, like the two Français rows. The organisation under the name tells them apart. The versions in the list are the newest on Door43, not the ones your project uses. To check in the downloaded language, choose it in Project settings. See Change the checking language. Offline, the dialog says "tC4 did not read the Door43 list of source texts." with Read the list. The line under it, "This organisation publishes nothing tC4 can use…", only means the list hasn't been read. If some downloads fail, the dialog lists them.

docs.title: Change the checking language
docs.summary: Choose which installed gateway language this project checks against.
docs.text: Checks use the notes and word articles of one gateway language. If the language isn't listed yet, download it first. See Download source texts. On Home, click Settings on the project card. Under Checking language, click the language you want. The current one is marked Current (1). Read the confirmation. It says how many decisions carry over and how many come back as work. Click "Change to …" to confirm. The new language is now marked Current. To cancel, click "Keep …" in the confirmation. A decision carries over only when the new notes have the same check on the same words. Notes in another language are often split differently, so few may carry over. That is expected. Nothing is deleted. Decisions that don't carry over stop counting, and those checks come back as To do. A finished book may not be finished any more. The language set must be complete: notes, words and academy. The same language can have two names, for example "Español (Latinoamérica)" in the list and "Spanish (Latin American)" in the confirmation.

docs.title: Update pinned helps
docs.summary: See whether newer notes, words and questions are out, and move your project to them when you are ready.
docs.text: A project keeps the exact versions it started with, so checks stay stable. Updating is always your choice. On Home, click Settings on the project card, then Manage source texts →. The project opens with Get source texts on top. Click Check for updates (1). If "Turn on the internet?" appears, click Turn on internet. See Working offline. Each set shows ✓ Up to date or "Upgrade N resource(s)" with each change, for example en_tn v86 → v91. Click "Upgrade N resource(s)", read the confirmation, and click Upgrade. To cancel, click Keep the current release. Decisions that match a check in the new release carry over. The rest come back as work. Nothing is deleted. A new project already uses the helps that come with the app, so it says ✓ Up to date. A project that checks in another language lists that language as the primary set and English as the fallback. tC4 doesn't check for updates by itself.

docs.title: Update scripture texts
docs.summary: Move the project to a newer release of the Greek or Hebrew text, or of the gateway Bible.
labels: ✓ Every scripture text is up to date
docs.text: On Home, click Settings on the project card, then Manage source texts →. The project opens with Get source texts on top. Click Check for updates (1). If "Turn on the internet?" appears, click Turn on internet. See Working offline. Look under Scripture texts. Each text with a newer release has its own row. Click Upgrade on a row, read the confirmation, and confirm. If everything is current, it says ✓ Every scripture text is up to date. Gateway Bible: nothing in your work changes. The source pane shows the new text. Greek or Hebrew text: alignments are kept, but the affected verses lose their valid mark so you can check them again. See Mark an alignment done. Only the texts your books need are offered. A New Testament project is never offered the Hebrew text. Save any open alignment edit first.

docs.title: Fix a missing resource
docs.summary: When a checking tool needs a resource that is not on this computer, tC4 offers three ways to get it.
docs.text: You usually see this with a project imported or copied from another computer. The tool card shows Needs downloading or Unavailable offline. In Check, click Fix this… on the tool card. Choose one way: 1 · Download the pinned version. Needs the internet. 2 · Use a version that is installed. Click a version, check how many decisions carry over, then click Re-pin. 3 · Sideload it from a file. Drop a Scripture Burrito zip of that exact release. To cancel, click Close or the ✕. Nothing changes. Offline, use option 2 or 3, or turn on the internet. See Working offline. A tool that isn't ready never blocks the rest of your work.

docs.title: Working offline
docs.summary: tC4 works without the internet. It asks before any step that needs it.
docs.text: Everything you need to translate and check with the English helps comes with the app, and your projects stay on your computer. Work as usual. No internet is needed. When a step needs the internet, tC4 asks "Turn on the internet?". Click Turn on internet (1), or Not now to stay offline. To turn the internet off again, click the round account button at the top right and switch off Use the internet (1). Closing tC4 also turns it off. Download source texts Update pinned helps and Update scripture texts Downloading a missing resource in Fix a missing resource Signing in and sharing on Door43 Translating, checking, aligning, exporting and importing all work offline. Nothing from your projects is sent when you turn the internet on for downloads. Keep regular backups of your projects folder. See Where your projects are stored.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.summary: Change a project’s text direction, script font or checking language, or manage its source texts.
docs.text: On Home, click Settings on the project card. Change what you need: Text direction: Left to right or Right to left. Checking language (1). See Change the checking language. Manage source texts → (2). See Download source texts. Script font (3): the font your translation is shown in. Click Save changes. To cancel, click Cancel or the ✕, or press Esc. Nothing is saved. The settings are only on the Home card, not in the top bar. To get back to Home, click the project name at the top left. The fonts are Noto Sans (default), Charis SIL, Scheherazade New (Arabic script), Awami Nastaliq (Nastaliq) and Padauk (Myanmar). Pick the one that shows your letters correctly. The name and language can't be changed yet: "Renaming arrives with a later increment."

docs.title: Where your projects are stored
docs.summary: tC4 keeps all your projects in one folder in your home folder. Back it up regularly.
docs.text: "Only on this computer" (1) on a project card means the project is stored only in this folder. System Folder Windows C:\Users\<you>\pankosmia\tc4-projects macOS ~/pankosmia/tc4-projects Linux ~/pankosmia/tc4-projects Close tC4. Copy the whole tc4-projects folder to a USB drive or another backup place. Uninstalling tC4 keeps your projects. To move one project to another computer, export a Scripture Burrito and import it there. That's safer than copying folders. Don't change files in the folder while tC4 is open. tC4 notices and stops to protect the project. See Messages that protect your project.

docs.title: Change the app language
docs.summary: Show translationCore's menus, buttons and dialogs in English, Spanish (Latin America), French or Hindi.
docs.text: Your translation and your projects do not change. Click the round person icon at the top right (1), then App language (2). The menu is the same on Home and inside a project. Click the Language box and choose a language. The whole app switches to that language right away, so you can see what it looks like before you decide. Click Apply to keep it. In Spanish the button reads Aplicar. To go back to the language you had, click Cancel or ✕ instead. translationCore remembers your choice the next time you open it. Changes: menus, buttons, labels and dialogs, such as Understand, Translate and Check at the top of a project. Doesn't change: your translation, the source texts (such as the ULT) and the translation helps (notes, words and questions). These stay in the language they were written in. To choose the language of the checking helps, see Checking language. If you can't read the current language, the person icon is always at the top right, and App language is the third item in its menu. English is always first in the list.

docs.title: When a save fails
docs.summary: If a save fails, your text stays on screen. Click Retry, and don’t close tC4 until it says Saved.
docs.text: The indicator at the top right shows Saved, Saving…, Unsaved changes or Save failed — retry. If you see Save failed — retry, click Retry once and wait. If it fails again, stay on the screen. Moving to another mode may be refused until the save works. If you try to close tC4 with unsaved changes, it warns you. Stay, and try Retry again. If it keeps failing, write down the message and ask for help. Clicking Retry many times doesn't help. It tries once at a time. In an imported project, writing the first text into an empty verse can fail to save every time. Retry won't fix it. Copy your text somewhere safe before you close tC4, because the verse comes back empty. Cancelling such a verse after typing can show the same message. ← All checking tools still works while a save problem is showing.

docs.title: Messages that protect your project
docs.summary: When tC4 finds something unexpected, it stops rather than risk your work, and tells you what to do.
headings: Messages when you open, save or export
docs.text: Each message says whether your work is saved, or that nothing was created. Read the message and follow its advice. For a refused import file, click ← Choose other files to pick a good file, or Cancel. If it says "Ask for help", contact your support person and leave the project folder as it is. Code Example What to do import.damaged.usfm-parse "no-id.sfm has no \id line, so the book is not known." Fix the file (for example add \id TIT as the first line), then choose it again. import.damaged.truncated "… is not a complete zip file." The zip was cut off. Export or copy it again. import.damaged.no-manifest "… has no manifest.json, so it is not a translationCore 3 project." Choose the zip translationCore 3 exported. import.damaged.corrupt-entry "… is damaged … so it cannot be read." Export it from translationCore 3 again. import.name-exists "A project with this name is already on this computer." Type another Bible name. import.write-failed "The partly written Bible was removed…" Try again. If it happens again, ask for help. Message starts with What to do "A file changed outside the app." Open the project again. tC4 repairs what it can and names what it can't. "A story file was changed outside the app." Undo the outside change, then open the project again. "This computer's change folder holds another computer's changes." A project folder was copied by hand. Ask for help. "… has no drafted verse yet, so the PDF has nothing to print." Draft at least one verse, then export again. "The app could not print the PDF…" Close tC4, open it again and export again. For stories, try with Pictures off. "The app stopped to protect your project." Ask for help. Write down the code, or take a picture of the message, when you ask for help. Under the red box the checks can still look green. Trust the red box: the file can't be imported.

docs.title: If the app closed unexpectedly or the window went blank
docs.summary: If tC4 closed unexpectedly or the window went blank, it recovers your projects. Window › Reload brings it back without quitting.
headings: If the window goes blank or stops responding
docs.text: tC4 records each step that changes a project. If it stops in the middle of one, it finishes or cleans up at the next start, so no broken project is left. Open the Window menu and click Reload, or press Ctrl+R. tC4 comes back on Home. Open your project again. If you see "This screen could not be shown.", click Back to Home, then open the project again. Start tC4 again. Check that your projects are on Home. If an import was interrupted, import the file again. Reload takes you to Home. Your projects are still there. Toggle Developer Tools is for developers. You don't need it.

docs.title: Windows, macOS and Linux notes
docs.summary: What to expect when you install and start tC4 on Windows, macOS and Linux.
docs.text: Test builds aren't signed yet, so your system may warn you the first time. System What to expect Windows SmartScreen may warn: click More info › Run anyway. You may need the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime. The plain USFM export may not download. macOS The first time, go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. Quit tC4 before you install another version. Linux Unzip and run start-tc4.sh. Follow Install and start tC4. If your system blocks it, follow its "open anyway" steps above. Run only one copy of tC4 at a time.

docs.title: Share to Door43
docs.summary: Put a project on Door43 so others can read it. You sign in once and review where it goes before anything is uploaded.
docs.text: Sharing sends the project to Door43. Later shares upload your changes again. Bible and Open Bible Stories projects share the same way. On Home, click Share on Door43 on the project card (1). tC4 asks "Turn on the internet?". Click Turn on internet (1). If you aren't signed in, sign in with your Door43 username or email and password. Choose your account or an organization, review the books, and upload. To cancel, click Not now or the ✕. Nothing is sent. You can also sign in from the round account button at the top right › Sign in to Door43. Tick Stay signed in on this computer if you don't want to sign in every time. Each change you share is signed with this computer's account name, which Door43 shows as the author. Sharing only sends. Bringing a project back from Door43 and team sync aren't built yet. See Working as a team on several computers.

docs.title: Working as a team on several computers
docs.summary: Each computer keeps its own copy of a project. Syncing a project between computers isn’t built yet.
docs.text: "Only on this computer" on a project card means just that: no other computer gets your changes automatically. Export a Scripture Burrito. They import it. Import always makes a new project. To let others read your work, share it on Door43. Bringing it back into tC4 isn't built yet. Don't copy project folders between computers by hand. tC4 will refuse to open them, to protect the project.

docs.title: Features not built yet
docs.summary: Things people often ask for that tC4 doesn’t do yet.
docs.text: This list is updated with each release. Feature Now Rename a project or change its language Not yet. "Renaming arrives with a later increment." Renumber verses Not yet Book introductions Not yet Footnotes in the PDF Not yet. The switch is shown but can't be turned on. Checking progress on Home Not yet. Home shows drafting progress only. Version history, or undo after you close tC4 Not yet Export checks as a spreadsheet Not yet Automatic update checks Not yet. Use Check for updates. See Update pinned helps. Import into an existing project USFM books only, with Add a book › Add books from USFM files. Other imports make a new project. Receive a project from Door43, team sync Not yet. Sending works: see Share to Door43. Right-to-left and complex scripts Work, with polish still to come

docs.title: alpha.1 — First public build
docs.summary: The first public snapshot of translationCore 4, a ground-up rewrite. Create a project and draft beside source texts.
docs.text: Draft: create a project, choose source texts, and draft beside them. See Start a new Bible project. Check and Align: work started, entering review. Format: every project is a Scripture Burrito. translationCore 3 is a separate program. Projects can now be imported (see Import a project), but tC3 versions do not carry over.

docs.title: alpha.2 — Check and align
docs.summary: Check a whole book with Translation Notes and Translation Words, and align verses to the original language.
docs.text: Check with Translation Notes and Translation Words, against resources pinned at exact versions. Align: link each word of a verse to the original language. Editing a verse marks its alignment for review.

docs.title: alpha.4 — Open and resume
docs.summary: Resume where you left off after a restart, checkpoints on mode changes, and the new design for Understand, Translate and Check.
docs.text: Resume across a restart: Home's Resume card returns you to the book and chapter. Checkpoints: saved when you switch mode or leave a project. "Checkpoint not saved" offers Retry. The Understand, Translate and Check workflow on the new design. Align rebuilt as a Check tool (with gateway and original modes). A progress bar while a project opens. This build shipped no English scripture; later builds include it.

docs.title: alpha.5 — Drafting for real
docs.summary: Draft a whole section at a time, place verse numbers, join verses into spans, format paragraphs and poetry, and read a passage with helps.
docs.text: Draft a section and place verse numbers. Verse spans such as 9-10 (Bible only). Paragraph and poetry formatting. The Greek or Hebrew text beside ULT and UST in Translate. Understand with notes, questions and user comments. The English resources ship with the app, so you can work offline from the first start. A Windows build.

docs.title: alpha.6 — Suggestions and resources
docs.summary: Alignment suggestions, check comments and bookmarks, resource upgrades, and a guided fix for missing resources.
docs.text: Alignment suggestions: off by default; you confirm or reject each. Mark an alignment done. Check comments and bookmarks. Update pinned helps with Check for updates. Fix a missing resource. Resume returns to the mode you last used. Installers for macOS (.pkg) and Windows (.exe). One Section/Verse switch in Translate; the helps panel follows the verses in focus. Windows needs the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime.

docs.title: alpha.7 — Open Bible Stories
docs.summary: Create an Open Bible Stories project, translate stories frame by frame with pictures, read them with helps, and check them.
docs.text: Start an Open Bible Stories project and find stories on Home. Translate a story frame by frame beside the pictures. Understand a story with notes, word links and questions per frame. Check a story with Translation Notes and Translation Words. The OBS resources and pictures ship with the app. A failed save retries one attempt at a time. The release notes said export was not built yet. It arrived in rc.1: see What's new in 4.0 rc.1.

docs.title: Sep 27, 2026 — one + Add a project button on Home
docs.summary: Home now has one + Add a project button instead of three. It opens a dialog where you choose a new Bible, new Open Bible Stories, or an import. The Home heading is now Your projects.
docs.text: Home's heading is now Your projects (it was "Your Bibles"). One blue + Add a project button replaces the separate buttons for a new Bible, new Open Bible Stories and import. + Add a project opens a dialog with three cards: New Bible, New Open Bible Stories and Import a project. See The Home screen. Each card opens the same form as before: Create a Bible project, Start an Open Bible Stories project, Import a project. Import step 1 has a ← Back button that returns to the three cards. With no projects yet, Home says "No projects yet. Select + Add a project to start." Keyboard: Tab moves through the cards, Enter or Space opens one, and Esc closes the dialog. After a form closes, the keyboard focus doesn't return to + Add a project. The New Bible form can be taller than a small window. Scroll inside it to reach Create Bible →.

docs.title: What's new in 4.0 rc.1
docs.summary: Get your work out and bring existing work in: export a book as PDF, USFM or a Scripture Burrito, export stories as Markdown, PDF or a burrito, and import translationCore 3, USFM and Scripture Burrito files. Plus project Settings on the Home card, new books opening in Understand, English helps v91 in the box, and Spacing and Paper size for printing.
docs.text: Export All exports start from Check › Community Checking › Open → › Export. When the file is saved, the panel says "Saved <file name>". Bible book: Export PDF, USFM, aligned, USFM, plain and Scripture Burrito (.zip). See Export a book as PDF, Export a book as USFM and Export a project as a Scripture Burrito. Open Bible Stories: Export PDF (with or without pictures), Story Markdown (.zip) and Scripture Burrito (.zip). See Export stories as PDF or Markdown. A book with nothing drafted isn't printed. tC4 tells you to draft at least one verse first. Import + Add a project › Import a project makes a new project from a translationCore 3 project, USFM files or a Scripture Burrito. See Import a project. The review shows the books, three checks (License, Details, Missing verses) and what carries over. A missing language code or a Bible name already in use must be fixed before you can import. Damaged files are refused with a reason and a code, and nothing is created. See Messages that protect your project. The new card has an Imported badge. Also new Settings on the card: click Settings on a project's Home card. See Project settings. A cleaner top bar. Cards say "Only on this computer" or where the project is shared. See The Home screen. New books open in Understand, so you read before you draft. After that a book reopens in the mode you used last. See The three modes. English helps v91 come with the app, so a new project needs no download. See What comes with the app. Moving between a Bible and a stories project no longer confuses their notes and words. See Check a story. Page setup for printing: spacing and paper size for Bible books, and picture layout for stories. See Community Checking preview and Story preview and export. Window › Reload (Ctrl+R) brings the app back without quitting. A screen that can't be drawn shows "This screen could not be shown." with Back to Home. See If the app closed unexpectedly. Resume returns to the last mode, including the checking tool you were using. See Resume where you left off. Check for updates offers only the texts your books need. A New Testament project isn't offered the Hebrew text. See Update scripture texts. Changing the checking language keeps the checks that still match. The rest come back as work; nothing is deleted. See Change the checking language. translationCore 3 imports ask whether to look up the resource versions on Door43 or use the ones on this computer. See Import a project. After you join verses into a span, the book's percentage can drop, and the Resume banner can still name the old verse. The "… was imported" message doesn't close by itself. Close it with its ✕. In USFM exports, the \h, \toc and \mt lines carry the book code (for example TIT), not the book name. On Linux, the save window's Save and Cancel buttons can be off-screen. Press Enter to save, or Esc to cancel. The same language can be named two ways, for example "Español (Latinoamérica)" in lists and "Spanish (Latin American)" in sentences.
